subject: PrivGPU tiling + egress capacity decision log
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@atlascloud.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: PrivGPU topology input: tiling and egress headroom

Maya,

Thanks again for the kickoff earlier. As discussed, we're drafting the private GPU pool topology and need final egress and peering constraints so we can size tiling and runway. Short ask below so we can close the sizing by EOW: 

- Confirm sustained outbound egress available from the VPC (Gbps) and any per-flow caps.
- Any cross-AZ bandwidth shaping or asymmetric egress rates we should account for?
- Can you confirm whether multicast/inner-cluster RPCs will be subject to the same per-tenant policing?

Attached is a working spreadsheet with our baseline throughput targets and a first-pass tiling scheme. Our initial goal: support 2.5M tokens/min sustained with 95th perc latency target 180ms. We expect bursts up to 6M tokens/min for ~5 minute windows.

If you can answer the three bullets and call out any platform-imposed headroom rules, that will let us finalize the tiling (pod-per-tenant vs shared tile) recommendation.

Thanks,
Mateo
Sr. SWE, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- privgpu-capacity-calcs-20251007.xlsx (baseline + assumptions)
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@atlascloud.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Ops <ops@atlascloud.com>
Date: 2025-10-07T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivGPU topology input: tiling and egress headroom

Mateo —

Quick answers inline: 

- Sustained outbound egress per VPC: 10 Gbps nominal (shared across account); we allow bursting to 18 Gbps for short windows but bursts > 12 Gbps need pre-approval.
- Cross-AZ: there is an internal cap of 6 Gbps per AZ pairing when traffic is forwarded through our transit fabric — recommend avoiding heavy cross-AZ KV traffic.
- Tenant policing: yes, per-tenant policing is enforced on egress ranges; default throttle applies at 4 Gbps per tenant. For enterprise customers we can raise to 8 Gbps with a reserved carveout (requires PO/contract amendment).

Notes: We saw similar systems get into trouble with KV syncs across AZs — suggest placing warm caches and primary tiles in the same AZ to reduce cross-AZ egress.

I'll attach a short PDF showing the egress envelope and suggested peering slots.

—Maya
AtlasCloud Ops

Attachments:
- atlas-egress-envelope-20251007.pdf
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-08T10:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivGPU topology input: tiling and egress headroom

Thanks Maya — useful detail. Mateo/Jonas/Karthik, quick internal sync based on AtlasCloud replies: 

Summary of constraints:
- VPC sustained egress: 10 Gbps; safe burst to 12 Gbps; pre-approve for 18 Gbps (rare).
- Per-tenant default policing: 4 Gbps; enterprise carveout to 8 Gbps with contract amendment.
- Cross-AZ pairwise cap: 6 Gbps — avoid heavy KV cross-AZ.

Implications for tiling and run rate: 
- With default 4 Gbps tenant cap, a single tile (one GPU pod) can reliably support ~350k tokens/min for typical embedding+completion mixes; we need to tile horizontally for the 2.5M sustained goal.
- Proposal: 8 tiles (pods) per tenant in AZ-local placement for steady-state (8 * 350k ≈ 2.8M tokens/min). Keep a small warm standby tile for fast failover.
- Burst strategy: enable short-lived autoscale boats that can spin up 6 additional tiles for 5 minute windows; these will require pre-approved egress carveout if we exceed tenant 8 Gbps.

Action items: 
1) Karthik — run the model with our latency SLO and the 4 Gbps tenant policing to produce a latency vs tile-count table (use the shared KV/cache residency assumption). Deadline: 10/09 EOD.
2) Jonas — draft the contract amendment language to request an 8 Gbps tenant carveout for ACME (include cost delta). Draft due 10/10.
3) Mateo — update the tiling diagram and attach the final calculations to the Drive link.

I'll keep AtlasCloud in the loop once we have the numbers to request the carveout.

Laura
Head of Private Ops
Redwood Inference

Date: 2025-10-09T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivGPU topology input: tiling and egress headroom — decisions and next steps

Maya / AtlasCloud ops,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the envelope PDF. Quick decision log and next steps from our side so everyone is aligned: 

Decisions made (10/09):
- Steady-state topology: 8 AZ-local tiles per tenant (primary + 7 active), one warm standby in the same AZ. This maps to ~2.8M tokens/min sustained with our workload mix.
- Burst plan: allow autoscale up to +6 tiles for 5-minute windows. We will submit a carveout request for an 8 Gbps per-tenant limit (to support burst headroom) and a temporary account-level pre-approval for bursts to 14 Gbps while the amendment is processed.
- Cross-AZ KV: avoid synchronous cross-AZ KV writes for hot state; adopt AZ affinity and replicate via async background sync.

Deliverables and owners: 
- Mateo: final tiling diagram + updated capacity spreadsheet (attached: tiling-proposal-v1.png; privgpu-capacity-calcs-20251007.xlsx) — due 10/10 11:59 PT.
- Karthik: latency vs tiles table (per Laura's ask) — due 10/09 EOD (please drop in the Drive link).
- Jonas: cost delta and draft amendment for 8 Gbps carveout — draft 10/10.
- Laura: coordinate with Sales/Legal to queue the carveout PO request once Jonas' draft is ready.

Follow-up: Mateo will open a HubSpot note (link below) and submitted DocuSign request for the temporary pre-approval. Maya, please confirm receipt and whether AtlasCloud needs any additional telemetry (flow logs, sample pcap) to speed the carveout approval.

Best,
Mateo
Sr. SWE, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
